title: Derived maps from locally finite free sheaves via hypercohomology
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ be a ringed site small under [def-weil-size-convention], with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P$ be an $R$-module sheaf such that every site object admits a covering on which $P$ is isomorphic to $R^{\oplus r}$ for finite nonnegative $r$ (ranks may vary between covering objects). Define $P^\vee=\mathcal Hom_R(P,R)$ using [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For every bounded-below complex $K^\bullet$ of $R$-module sheaves and every integer $n$ there is a canonical isomorphism of abelian groups $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(P[0],QK[n])\cong H^n(R\Gamma(\mathcal C,P^\vee\otimes_R K^\bullet))$, where tensor is termwise sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $Q$ is localization, and derived global sections are computed by a bounded-below injective resolution. The isomorphism is natural in $P$, in $K$, and in shifts; it is induced by evaluation $P^\vee\otimes_RP\to R$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, label lemma-dual-perfect-complex, the final displayed global Hom formula, specialized to the perfect object P[0]; local finite freeness identifies the derived tensor with termwise tensor.

proof.text: For any module sheaf $F$, define $a_F:P^\vee\otimes_R F\to\mathcal Hom_R(P,F)$ by $\lambda\otimes f\mapsto(p\mapsto\lambda(p)f)$. The formula is balanced and restriction-compatible, so descends through tensor sheafification. On a slice where $P\cong R^{\oplus r}$, let $e_j,e_j^\vee$ be the basis and dual basis. The inverse sends $h$ to $\sum_{j=1}^r e_j^\vee\otimes h(e_j)$; both composites are the identity. Thus $a_F$ is locally bijective and hence an isomorphism of sheaves, with an $R$-linear inverse. In particular $P^\vee$ is locally finite free. This construction uses evaluation, and applies termwise to complexes since $a_F$ commutes with maps of $F$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, final finite-free evaluation calculation

proof.text: The functor $T(F)=\mathcal Hom_R(P,F)$ is exact. Restriction to a slice is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. On each trivializing slice the cited finite-free Hom statement identifies an applied short exact sequence with its finite direct sum, which is exact. Exactness descends from these slices: kernels are sectionwise, and images and cokernels are sheafifications of sectionwise images and cokernels; a kernel section lifts to an image section locally on each slice, and the composite coverings give the required local lift on the original object. Vanishing of a kernel or cokernel is detected by the sheaf uniqueness axiom on those coverings. Therefore $T$ preserves kernels, images and cohomology of complexes; specifically $H^j(TA)=T(H^j(A))$. Step 1 identifies $T$ with $P^\vee\otimes_R-$, so this tensor functor is exact. Repeating the finite-free argument for $P^\vee$ identifies $\mathcal Hom_R(P^\vee,F)$ with $P\otimes_R F$ (the local bidual map sends $e_j$ to its double dual), hence $P\otimes_R-$ is exact as well. Consequently $P[0]$ is K-flat: its total tensor with an acyclic complex $A$ has terms $A^j\otimes_RP$ and zero cohomology by exactness.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, final finite-free calculation; Tag 03DA, sites-modules-lemma-abelian, for the local kernel/cokernel test; Tag 06YN, definition-K-flat

proof.text: Choose a quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to I$ with $I$ bounded below and degreewise injective, hence K-injective, by the cited resolution theorem. Exactness in step 2 makes $T(s):T(K)\to T(I)$ a quasi-isomorphism: $H^j(T(s))=T(H^j(s))$. Since $P$ is in degree zero, the Hom-complex definition gives $J=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P[0],I)=T(I)$, with $J^j=\mathcal Hom_R(P,I^j)$ and differential $h\mapsto d_Ih$. The cited K-flat-to-K-injective Hom lemma applies to $P[0]$ and $I$, and shows that $J$ is K-injective. It is also bounded below. Thus the composite $P^\vee\otimes_R K\xrightarrow{a_K}T(K)\xrightarrow{T(s)}J$ represents the desired complex by a bounded-below K-injective complex.

source.place: Tags 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective) and 0A8X (section-hom-complexes); bounded-below injective resolution as in Tag 07A5

proof.text: The computation by $J$ agrees with the stipulated bounded-below injective computation of derived global sections. Indeed choose $J\to B$ with $B$ bounded below and degreewise injective by the cited resolution theorem. Both $J$ and $B$ are K-injective, so their quasi-isomorphism is a homotopy equivalence by the cited derived-Hom comparison. Applying $\Gamma$ preserves the homotopy equations termwise. Hence $H^n(R\Gamma(\mathcal C,P^\vee\otimes_RK))$ is canonically $H^n(\Gamma(\mathcal C,J))$, for every integer $n$, and is independent of the choices. No assertion that $J$ is degreewise injective, and no exactness of global sections, is needed.

By [def-pur-sheaf-hom], $\Gamma(\mathcal C,J^j)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,I^j)$, with differential given by postcomposition with $d_I$. A degree-$n$ cycle in $\Gamma J$ is an $R$-linear map $f:P\to I^n$ with $d_If=0$, and a boundary is $d_Ih$ for $h:P\to I^{n-1}$. This is precisely a chain map $P[0]\to I[n]$ modulo chain homotopy: the differential in $I[n]$ is $(-1)^n d_I$, so the boundaries from homotopies differ only by the invertible sign $(-1)^n$. Addition of cycles corresponds to addition of maps. Therefore $H^n(\Gamma J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(R)}(P[0],I[n])$ additively. The cited shift theorem says $I[n]$ is K-injective, and the derived-Hom comparison identifies this group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(P[0],QI[n])$. Postcompose with $(Qs[n])^{-1}$ to obtain $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(P[0],QK[n])$. Compose with step 4 and invert to get the isomorphism in the statement.

For $u:P\to P'$ and a target chain map $v:I\to I'$, a cycle $f:P'\to I^n$ is sent to $v^n f u$. On tensors this same map is $u^\vee\otimes v$: for local sections $\lambda$ of $(P')^\vee$ and $x$ of $I^n$, evaluating $u^\vee(\lambda)\otimes v^n(x)$ at a local section $p$ of $P$ gives $\lambda(u(p))v^n(x)$, which equals $v^n(\lambda(u(p))x)$ by $R$-linearity. Thus the evaluation comparison and the cycle-to-chain-map identification commute with both variables. For a derived morphism $g:QK\to QK'$, the derived-Hom comparison gives a unique homotopy class $v:I\to I'$ representing $Qs'\,g\,(Qs)^{-1}$; if $v-w=d_{I'}h+h d_I$, then $T(v)-T(w)=T(d_{I'})T(h)+T(h)T(d_I)$ because $T$ is additive and preserves composition. Applying $\Gamma$ gives the same homotopy equation, so the two maps induce identical maps on cohomology. This also proves choice independence and naturality for derived morphisms. For a shift $m$, use $s[m]:K[m]\to I[m]$, a K-injective resolution by the shift theorem: $T(I[m])=T(I)[m]$ termwise and both differentials are $(-1)^m T(d_I)$. Reindexing a cycle $P\to I^{n+m}$ therefore gives the same map under $H^n(R\Gamma(TK[m]))=H^{n+m}(R\Gamma(TK))$ and $(QK[m])[n]\cong QK[n+m]$. These equations give the claimed compatibility with shifts and show the canonical isomorphism is induced by evaluation.
